questions.text: Match each key component of the technopreneurship ecosystem to what it includes.
allChoices: Researchers and thinkers, developers, marketers, and financiers
Science parks, incubation centers, universities, R&D centers, and reliable internet access
IPR offices, technology licensing, and legal services
Angel investors, venture capitalists, funding agencies, and financial services

pairs.match: Researchers and thinkers, developers, marketers, and financiers
Science parks, incubation centers, universities, R&D centers, and reliable internet access
IPR offices, technology licensing, and legal services
Angel investors, venture capitalists, funding agencies, and financial services

questions.explanation: Human Resources are the people (researchers and thinkers who generate ideas, developers who build, marketers who promote, financiers who manage money). Environment is the physical and digital spaces. Laws and Policies protect inventions and guide operations. Financial Resources supply seed money to launch and scale ventures.

questions.text: Which of the following are listed under the Human Resources (People) component of the ecosystem?
options: Researchers and thinkers who generate new ideas
questions.explanation: Human Resources includes researchers and thinkers, developers, marketers, and financiers who manage money. Venture capitalists belong to Financial Resources, and technology licensing belongs to Laws and Policies.

questions.text: Under which ecosystem component does "reliable internet access" fall?
questions.explanation: Environment (Infrastructure) includes physical and digital spaces like science parks, incubation centers, universities, R&D centers, and reliable internet access.

questions.text: According to the module, what is the purpose of Support Infrastructures?
options: To replace government regulation of startups
To buy equity in mature companies
To help lower entry barriers for early-stage ventures
To enforce patent and trademark rights in court
questions.explanation: Support Infrastructures help lower entry barriers for early-stage ventures.

questions.text: Match each support infrastructure to its description.
allChoices: Subsidized office space, shared administrative services, and technical mentorship during early validation stages
Affordable access to advanced laboratories, industrial testing equipment, and university-grade machinery
The digital connective tissue of the ecosystem, enabling tracking, matching, and regulatory registration

pairs.match: Subsidized office space, shared administrative services, and technical mentorship during early validation stages
Affordable access to advanced laboratories, industrial testing equipment, and university-grade machinery
The digital connective tissue of the ecosystem, enabling tracking, matching, and regulatory registration

questions.explanation: TBIs provide subsidized office space, shared admin services and technical mentorship. R&D Facilities & Science Parks give access to labs, testing equipment and machinery. Digital Infrastructure Platforms serve as the ecosystem's digital connective tissue.

questions.text: Technology Business Incubators in the Philippines are heavily driven by university partnerships. Which of the following are named as those university partnerships?
questions.explanation: The university partnerships named are UST TOMASInno Center, DLSU Animo Labs, and UP-Enterprise. QBO Innovation Hub is given as a public-private network, and the Startup Philippines Portal is a digital infrastructure platform.

questions.text: The QBO Innovation Hub is given as an example of which kind of incubator network?
questions.explanation: TBIs are driven by university partnerships alongside public-private networks (QBO Innovation Hub).

questions.text: R&D Facilities & Science Parks are accelerated through which program's nodes across regional universities?
questions.explanation: R&D Facilities & Science Parks are accelerated through the DOST Science for Change Program (S4CP) nodes across regional universities.

questions.text: The Startup Philippines Portal, a centralized platform where founders, investors, and accelerators register to access national benefits, is found at ___ (web address).
questions.explanation: The Startup Philippines Portal is startup.gov.ph, given as the example of a Digital Infrastructure Platform.

questions.text: According to the module, what do Support Programs deliver?
options: Subsidized office space and shared administrative services
Equity investments in exchange for board seats
Structured capacity building, non-equity financial runway, and legal framework navigation to scale ventures
Physical laboratories and industrial testing equipment
questions.explanation: Support Programs deliver structured capacity building, non-equity financial runway, and legal framework navigation to scale ventures.

questions.text: Match each support program to what it focuses on.
allChoices: Early-stage R&D, prototype enhancement, and solving technical hurdles
Commercialization, regional market expansion, and business scaling
Multi-week intensive programs that refine business models and provide investor readiness training
Focused growth tracks that boost underrepresented founders

pairs.match: Early-stage R&D, prototype enhancement, and solving technical hurdles
Commercialization, regional market expansion, and business scaling
Multi-week intensive programs that refine business models and provide investor readiness training
Focused growth tracks that boost underrepresented founders

questions.explanation: The DOST SGF backs early-stage R&D, prototypes and technical hurdles. DTI & DICT Match Funds focus on commercialization, regional expansion and scaling. Structured Mentorship refines business models, trains for investor readiness and grants access to corporate networks. Targeted Inclusivity tracks like WHWISE boost underrepresented founders.

questions.text: The DOST Startup Grant Fund and the DTI & DICT Match Funds are forms of equity funding, so the government takes ownership shares in the startup.
questions.explanation: They are listed under Government Grant Programs (Non-Equity Funding).

questions.text: What does WHWISE stand for?
options: Women Helping Women Innovating Social Enterprises
Women in High-Tech Working for Innovative Startup Enterprises
Workforce Hub for Women in Science and Engineering
Women Helping Women in Startup Ecosystems
questions.explanation: WHWISE is the Women Helping Women Innovating Social Enterprises program, a Targeted Inclusivity growth track.

questions.text: The Innovative Startup Act, the legal foundation providing operational subsidies, travel grants, startup visas, and tax incentives, is Republic Act No. ___.
questions.explanation: The Innovative Startup Act is RA 11337.

questions.text: Which of the following does the Innovative Startup Act (RA 11337) provide, according to the module?
options: Free office space in every TBI
questions.explanation: RA 11337 provides operational subsidies, travel grants, startup visas, and tax incentives.

questions.text: Under Legal & Policy Enablers, what does Intellectual Property (IP) Assistance offer?
options: Automatic copyright certificates for all software
Fast-tracked patent and trademark filing support to secure core technological assets
questions.explanation: IP Assistance is fast-tracked patent and trademark filing support to secure core technological assets.

questions.text: The incubator "does not just rent out cheap desks." Match each quality of a high-value incubator to its description.
allChoices: Direct access to technical experts, alumni founders, IP attorneys, and certified public accountants
Connections with academic institutions, government agencies, and corporate allies
A data-driven, agile management team with deep insight into emerging tech trends
An immersive environment for peer-to-peer learning, cross-disciplinary partnerships, and open innovation

pairs.term: An Extensive and Elite Mentor Network
pairs.match: Direct access to technical experts, alumni founders, IP attorneys, and certified public accountants
Connections with academic institutions, government agencies, and corporate allies
A data-driven, agile management team with deep insight into emerging tech trends
An immersive environment for peer-to-peer learning, cross-disciplinary partnerships, and open innovation

questions.explanation: The incubator operates as an active, high-value ecosystem enabler through its mentor network, institutional integration, leadership that goes beyond traditional administrative oversight, and a resource-rich culture.

questions.text: Under Deep Institutional and Ecosystem Integration, the incubator cultivates connections with three groups. Match each group to what it provides.
allChoices: Research pipelines
Non-dilutive funding
Early customer validation

pairs.match: Research pipelines
Non-dilutive funding
Early customer validation

questions.explanation: The incubator connects with regional academic institutions for research pipelines, government agencies for non-dilutive funding, and corporate allies for early customer validation.

questions.text: According to the module, what dictates the overall success rate of an incubation facility?
options: The size of its office space
The quality and behavior of the cohort selected for incubation
The number of government grants it receives
How many patents its mentors hold
questions.explanation: The quality and behavior of the cohort selected for incubation dictate the overall success rate of the facility.

questions.text: Match each trait of successful incubatees to its description.
allChoices: Building something people actually want, with clear focus and no administrative busywork
Testing assumptions rapidly, embracing fast failure, and adjusting the business model from user feedback
A small, highly adaptive team willing to wear multiple operational hats

pairs.match: Building something people actually want, with clear focus and no administrative busywork
Testing assumptions rapidly, embracing fast failure, and adjusting the business model from user feedback
A small, highly adaptive team willing to wear multiple operational hats

questions.explanation: Efficient Product Discovery means building something people want while avoiding peripheral distractions. Agility means testing assumptions, embracing fast failure and adjusting from user feedback. A Hungry, Fully-Dedicated Core Team is small, adaptive, and wears multiple hats to push the technology forward.

questions.text: How large are early startup teams typically, according to the module?
questions.explanation: Early startup teams are small, typically 1 to 4 people.

questions.text: A successful incubation process requires teams to avoid failure at all costs and keep their original business model unchanged.
questions.explanation: Under Agility and Openness to Pivoting, teams must test assumptions rapidly, embrace fast failure, and smoothly adjust their business model based on user feedback.

questions.text: A successful incubation program tracks clear Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) to monitor its ongoing what?
questions.explanation: A successful incubation program tracks clear KPIs to monitor its ongoing return on investment (ROI).

questions.text: Match each performance metric to its definition.
allChoices: The predictable, total revenue generated monthly from all active subscriptions
An annualized projection of current recurring revenue, assuming constant customer volume and pricing
The proportion of revenue remaining after deducting the direct costs of producing and delivering goods or services
The total sales and marketing spending required to acquire a single new customer in a period
The total projected gross profit expected from one customer account over the entire relationship
Compares the total value derived from a customer against the cost incurred to acquire them

pairs.match: The predictable, total revenue generated monthly from all active subscriptions
An annualized projection of current recurring revenue, assuming constant customer volume and pricing
The proportion of revenue remaining after deducting the direct costs of producing and delivering goods or services
The total sales and marketing spending required to acquire a single new customer in a period
The total projected gross profit expected from one customer account over the entire relationship
Compares the total value derived from a customer against the cost incurred to acquire them

questions.explanation: MRR is monthly revenue from active subscriptions. ARR annualizes recurring revenue. Gross Margin is what remains after COGS. CAC is the sales and marketing cost per new customer. LTV is the projected gross profit over the whole customer relationship. LTV to CAC compares customer value against acquisition cost.

questions.text: Match each metric to its formula.
allChoices: Total Number of Active Customers × ARPU
MRR × 12
[(Total Revenue − COGS) ÷ Total Revenue] × 100
Total Sales & Marketing Expenses ÷ New Customers Acquired
ARPU × Customer Lifetime (months) × Gross Margin %
Total Revenue ÷ Total Active Users

pairs.match: Total Number of Active Customers × ARPU
MRR × 12
[(Total Revenue − COGS) ÷ Total Revenue] × 100
Total Sales & Marketing Expenses ÷ New Customers Acquired
ARPU × Customer Lifetime (months) × Gross Margin %
Total Revenue ÷ Total Active Users

questions.explanation: These are the formulas as given in the module: MRR = active customers × ARPU, ARR = MRR × 12, Gross Margin = [(Revenue − COGS) ÷ Revenue] × 100, CAC = S&M expenses ÷ new customers, LTV = ARPU × lifetime (months) × Gross Margin %, and ARPU = Total Revenue ÷ Total Active Users.

questions.text: A startup has 2,000 active customers and an ARPU of ₱500. What is its Monthly Recurring Revenue (MRR)?
questions.explanation: MRR = Total Number of Active Customers × ARPU = 2,000 × ₱500 = ₱1,000,000.

questions.text: A startup's MRR is ₱450,000. What is its Annual Run Rate (ARR)?
A startup earns ₱800,000 in total revenue, and its cost of goods sold (COGS) is ₱200,000. What is its Gross Margin?
A startup spent ₱600,000 on sales and marketing and acquired 1,500 new customers in the same period. What is its Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC)?
questions.explanation: CAC = Total Sales & Marketing Expenses ÷ New Customers Acquired = ₱600,000 ÷ 1,500 = ₱400.

questions.text: A customer has an ARPU of ₱250 per month, stays for 20 months, and the gross margin is 60%. What is the Customer Lifetime Value (LTV)?
questions.explanation: LTV = ARPU × Customer Lifetime (months) × Gross Margin % = ₱250 × 20 × 0.60 = ₱3,000.

questions.text: What is the industry benchmark target for the LTV to CAC ratio?
questions.explanation: The industry benchmark is a target ratio of 3:1 or higher.

questions.text: What does an LTV to CAC ratio of 1:1 signify?
options: The startup has reached product-market fit
Revenue is entirely depleted by acquisition costs
The startup should cut its gross margin
questions.explanation: A 1:1 ratio signifies revenue is entirely depleted by acquisition costs.

questions.text: A startup's LTV is ₱3,000 and its CAC is ₱1,000. How does it compare with the industry benchmark?
options: It falls below the benchmark, at 1:3
It falls below the benchmark, since only 1:1 is acceptable
It can't be judged without the ARR
It meets the benchmark, at exactly 3:1
questions.explanation: LTV ÷ CAC = ₱3,000 ÷ ₱1,000 = 3:1, which meets the target of 3:1 or higher.

questions.text: What does ARPU stand for?
options: Average Revenue Per User (Average Revenue Per Unit)
questions.explanation: ARPU is Average Revenue Per User (Average Revenue Per Unit), a fundamental unit economics metric for evaluating platform revenue per active customer.

questions.text: In the BayadPo scenario, what does BayadPo's mobile app allow Sari-Sari stores to do?
questions.explanation: BayadPo is a homegrown tech startup whose app lets Sari-Sari stores across Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao order digital inventory, accept QR payments, and disburse micro-loans to community members.

questions.text: In August, BayadPo earned ₱12,500,000 in total revenue from 50,000 monthly active store owners. What is its monthly ARPU?
questions.explanation: ARPU = Total Revenue ÷ Total Active Users = ₱12,500,000 ÷ 50,000 = ₱250 / user / month.

questions.text: Match each reason the ₱250 ARPU is actionable for BayadPo to its point.
allChoices: Philippine tech platforms target sheer volume over high individual prices, so modest per-store revenue still adds up to massive velocity
Spending more to acquire a store than it returns monthly means the user must stay for months just to pay off ad spend
New features like micro-insurance or bill payments let current users spend more inside the system

pairs.match: Philippine tech platforms target sheer volume over high individual prices, so modest per-store revenue still adds up to massive velocity
Spending more to acquire a store than it returns monthly means the user must stay for months just to pay off ad spend
New features like micro-insurance or bill payments let current users spend more inside the system

questions.explanation: The mass-market strategy is validated by aggregate scale (₱12.5 Million/month). The ARPU sets hard limits on marketing (CAC). And cross-selling new features raises ARPU without needing millions of new users.

questions.text: Under "Hard Marketing Limits," why is spending ₱300 to acquire one store dangerous for BayadPo?
options: Because Facebook ads are banned for fintech apps
Because the store will immediately switch to a competitor
Because each store only returns ₱250 gross revenue monthly, so the user must stick around for months just to pay off the ad spend
Because ₱300 is above the legal CAC limit set by RA 11337
questions.explanation: Spending ₱300 to acquire one store is dangerous if they only return ₱250 gross revenue monthly. The user must stick around for months just to pay off ad spend.

questions.text: Under "Cross-Selling Push," how can BayadPo lift its ARPU from ₱250 to ₱350?
options: By rolling out new features, like integrated micro-insurance or bill payments, so current users spend an extra ₱100/month
By acquiring millions of new users immediately
By raising the price of its existing service for all stores
By cutting its marketing budget to zero
questions.explanation: Management doesn't need millions of new users immediately. Rolling out new features like integrated micro-insurance or bill payments lets current users spend an extra ₱100/month inside the system.

questions.text: To qualify as a genuine innovation, an idea must satisfy three core pillars. Match each pillar to its requirement.
allChoices: The concept must be new, or applied in a substantially innovative manner within its target context
The idea must go beyond theory, patents, or preliminary designs to full development, launch, and practical application
The initiative must generate demonstrable benefits, such as efficiency, lower costs, more revenue, or human well-being

pairs.match: The concept must be new, or applied in a substantially innovative manner within its target context
The idea must go beyond theory, patents, or preliminary designs to full development, launch, and practical application
The initiative must generate demonstrable benefits, such as efficiency, lower costs, more revenue, or human well-being

questions.explanation: The three core pillars of innovation are Novelty, Implementation, and Value Creation.

questions.text: An idea that exists only as a patent or a preliminary design already qualifies as a genuine innovation.
questions.explanation: Under the Implementation pillar, the idea must transcend theoretical concepts, patents, or preliminary designs, advancing to full development, official launch, and practical application.

questions.text: Innovation by Business Dimension: match each type to its example.
allChoices: Tesla creating electric vehicles with autonomous driving capabilities
Amazon using automated Kiva robots in fulfillment centers to pick and pack orders faster
Spotify shifting music from buying individual albums to an all-you-can-listen monthly subscription

pairs.match: Tesla creating electric vehicles with autonomous driving capabilities
Amazon using automated Kiva robots in fulfillment centers to pick and pack orders faster
Spotify shifting music from buying individual albums to an all-you-can-listen monthly subscription

questions.explanation: Product/Service Innovation introduces a new or significantly improved good or service (Tesla). Process Innovation changes how a product is made, delivered, or supported (Amazon's Kiva robots). Business Model Innovation re-engineers how a company creates, delivers, and captures value (Spotify's subscription).

questions.text: A company changes its pricing structure and target demographic to change how it creates, delivers, and captures value. Which type of innovation is this?
questions.explanation: Business Model Innovation is re-engineering how a company creates, delivers, and captures value, such as changing pricing structure or target demographic.

questions.text: Who coined the "By Market Impact" classification of innovation (Sustaining vs. Disruptive)?
questions.explanation: Innovation by Market Impact was coined by Clayton Christensen, looking at how innovation alters the competitive landscape.

questions.text: A razor company adds a 5th blade or a lubricating strip to an existing razor line. Which type of innovation is this?
questions.explanation: Sustaining Innovation caters to high-end customers in existing markets by making good products better, strictly following the established rules of the industry.

questions.text: Which statement describes Disruptive Innovation?
options: It makes good products better for high-end customers in existing markets
It makes minor modifications to existing components while keeping the architecture intact
It introduces a simpler, more affordable, or convenient alternative, starting with low-end or unserved customers before moving upmarket and displacing industry leaders
It strictly follows the established rules of the industry
questions.explanation: Disruptive Innovation introduces a simpler, more affordable, or convenient alternative, targeting low-end or unserved customers first. The module's example is digital photography apps and smartphone cameras eliminating consumer film cameras (Kodak).

questions.text: Henderson-Clark Model: match each type of innovation to its definition.
allChoices: Minor modifications to existing components while keeping the established architecture intact
Complete replacement of a core component while preserving the overall system structure
Reconfigures linkages and relationships among unchanged individual components
Comprehensive overhaul of both core components and architectural connections

pairs.match: Minor modifications to existing components while keeping the established architecture intact
Complete replacement of a core component while preserving the overall system structure
Reconfigures linkages and relationships among unchanged individual components
Comprehensive overhaul of both core components and architectural connections

questions.explanation: The Henderson-Clark Model (By Tech vs. Market Nuance) examines how innovation impacts core components versus the overarching system architecture.

questions.text: Henderson-Clark Model: match each example to its type of innovation.
allChoices: Incremental Innovation
Modular Innovation
Architectural Innovation
Radical Innovation

pairs.term: Integrating a faster microchip into an existing smartphone model
pairs.match: Incremental Innovation

pairs.term: Replacing a gas engine with an electric motor inside an existing car frame
pairs.match: Modular Innovation

pairs.term: Reorganizing standard computing hardware into a cloud server architecture
pairs.match: Architectural Innovation

pairs.term: The shift from mechanical typewriters to digital word processing systems
pairs.match: Radical Innovation

questions.explanation: Faster microchip: Incremental. Gas engine to electric motor in the same frame: Modular. Standard hardware reorganized into cloud architecture: Architectural. Typewriters to digital word processing: Radical.

questions.text: The New Products Classification from the Consumer's Viewpoint was proposed by whom?
questions.explanation: The Consumer's Viewpoint classification (Continuous, Dynamically Continuous, Discontinuous) was proposed by Thomas Robertson.

questions.text: Robertson's classification: match each type of new product to its level and customer impact.
allChoices: Most common; Zero Behavioral Friction
Moderate disruption; Low-to-Moderate Learning Curve
Rarest and high impact; Massive Learning Curve

pairs.match: Most common; Zero Behavioral Friction
Moderate disruption; Low-to-Moderate Learning Curve
Rarest and high impact; Massive Learning Curve

questions.explanation: Continuous Innovation is the most common, with zero behavioral friction. Dynamically Continuous involves moderate disruption and a low-to-moderate learning curve. Discontinuous is the rarest and highest impact, with a massive learning curve.

questions.text: Robertson's classification: match each example to its type of new product.
allChoices: Continuous Innovation
Dynamically Continuous Innovation
Discontinuous Innovation

pairs.term: The iPhone 17 Pro replacing the iPhone 16 Pro
pairs.match: Continuous Innovation

pairs.term: A laundry detergent adding a "lemon fresh" scent option
pairs.match: Continuous Innovation

pairs.term: Switching from keys to a smart fingerprint door lock
pairs.match: Dynamically Continuous Innovation

pairs.term: Migrating from standard cable TV to streaming apps
pairs.match: Dynamically Continuous Innovation
Discontinuous Innovation

pairs.term: The birth of commercial internet browsers
pairs.match: Discontinuous Innovation

questions.explanation: Continuous examples: a new soft drink flavor, the iPhone 17 Pro replacing the 16 Pro, a lemon-fresh detergent. Dynamically Continuous: manual to electric sonic toothbrushes, keys to fingerprint locks, cable TV to streaming. Discontinuous: the automobile (replacing horses), the personal computer (replacing typewriters), commercial internet browsers.

questions.text: Which type of new product requires extensive customer education because it introduces a brand-new concept, technology, and habit?
questions.explanation: Discontinuous Innovation creates severe disruption, completely overhauls consumer behavior, and requires extensive customer education.

questions.text: In Dynamically Continuous Innovation, the core utility or purpose stays familiar, but the technology, method, or design forces users to slightly adapt their behavior.
questions.explanation: Dynamically Continuous Innovation involves moderate disruption: users must adapt to a new mechanism to achieve a familiar goal.

questions.text: How does the module define Seed Money (Seed Capital)?
options: The final round of funding before a company goes public
A government grant that never has to be repaid
The earliest stage of institutional funding a startup raises to move from a conceptual product to a validated business model
Personal savings the founders put in before registering the business
questions.explanation: Seed money is the earliest stage of institutional funding that a startup raises to transition from a conceptual product to a validated business model.

questions.text: What is the average capital raised in a seed round, according to the module?
questions.explanation: The average seed capital raised is $500,000 to $3,000,000+. High-technology sectors, such as generative artificial intelligence, may secure substantially larger seed rounds.

questions.text: Seed capital is commonly structured through investor-friendly instruments. Match each instrument to its description.
allChoices: An investor provides capital in exchange for the right to acquire equity during a later priced financing round
Short-term debt instruments that automatically convert into equity at the next major financing round

pairs.match: An investor provides capital in exchange for the right to acquire equity during a later priced financing round
Short-term debt instruments that automatically convert into equity at the next major financing round

questions.explanation: A SAFE gives the investor the right to acquire equity in a subsequent priced round. Convertible Notes are short-term debt that converts into equity at the next major financing round.

questions.text: Seed capital is most commonly distributed as direct cash in exchange for common stock.
questions.explanation: Seed capital is infrequently distributed as direct cash for common stock. It is commonly structured through flexible instruments like SAFEs and Convertible Notes.

questions.text: Capital raised during the seed stage is targeted toward which key milestones?
options: Core Team: establishing a core leadership and engineering team
Initial Scaling: scaling engineering and marketing to acquire initial paying customers
Listing the company on the stock exchange
questions.explanation: The primary usage of seed capital is the Core Team, Product-Market Fit (PMF), and Initial Scaling.

questions.text: Match each type of intellectual property to what it protects in tech.
allChoices: Functional inventions, hardware designs, novel processes, or software architectures that produce a tangible technical result
The expression of an idea, not the idea itself
Brand identity, logos, business names, and distinct phrases
Confidential business information that provides a competitive edge

pairs.match: Functional inventions, hardware designs, novel processes, or software architectures that produce a tangible technical result
The expression of an idea, not the idea itself
Brand identity, logos, business names, and distinct phrases
Confidential business information that provides a competitive edge

questions.explanation: Patents protect functional inventions. Copyrights protect the expression of an idea. Trademarks protect brand identity. Trade Secrets protect confidential business information.

questions.text: According to the module, how do patents apply to software?
options: Software code itself is generally not patentable in most jurisdictions; patents protect the system architecture, logic flow, or data processing method
Software code itself is always patentable
Software can only be protected as a trade secret
questions.explanation: Software code itself is generally not patentable in most jurisdictions. Instead, patents protect the system architecture, logic flow, or data processing method.

questions.text: Which type of IP is the primary legal mechanism protecting your software source code, UI visuals, marketing content, and internal documentation?
questions.explanation: Copyright is the primary legal mechanism protecting software source code, user interface (UI) visuals, marketing content, and internal documentation.

questions.text: Which of the following are given as examples of trade secrets?
questions.explanation: The trade secret examples are source code repositories, mathematical algorithm weights, unpatented backend processes, and customer databases. The app name and logo are trademarks, and marketing content is covered by copyright.

questions.text: How are trade secrets protected, according to the module?
options: Through operational cybersecurity and mandatory legal contracts (NDAs)
Automatically, the moment they are written down
questions.explanation: Trade secrets are protected through operational cybersecurity and mandatory legal contracts (NDAs).

questions.text: Under the Startup Strategy Rule of Thumb, what should the primary IP tools be for a standard application like a regular e-commerce delivery app?
questions.explanation: For standard applications, Copyright and Trademarks are your primary tools to secure your code, custom visuals, and marketplace identity without excessive legal overhead.

questions.text: Under the Startup Strategy Rule of Thumb, when should a startup take the long, expensive path of patent filing?
options: Only when protecting a logo or app name
Only for deep-tech innovations, such as advanced AI model architectures or hardware integrations
Only after the app reaches 1 million users
questions.explanation: The patent filing path is reserved strictly for deep-tech innovations, such as advanced AI model architectures or hardware integrations, when your software contains highly complex, breakthrough processing mechanics.

questions.text: Match each crucial IP risk for tech startups to its description.
allChoices: IP rights go to whoever files first, not who invented first, so delaying registration lets competitors claim your architecture
Showcasing a prototype at a hackathon, pitch competition, or demo day before filing can permanently destroy patent novelty
Using open-source libraries without checking their licenses can force your entire proprietary suite to become open-source

pairs.match: IP rights go to whoever files first, not who invented first, so delaying registration lets competitors claim your architecture
Showcasing a prototype at a hackathon, pitch competition, or demo day before filing can permanently destroy patent novelty
Using open-source libraries without checking their licenses can force your entire proprietary suite to become open-source

questions.explanation: The three crucial IP risks are the First-to-File Rule, Public Disclosure Traps, and Third-Party Code Liability (e.g., GPL or MIT licenses).

questions.text: In the Philippines, patents and trademarks are granted to whoever invented first, regardless of who files first.
questions.explanation: In the Philippines and most international jurisdictions, IP rights (especially patents and trademarks) are granted to the person or entity that files first, not who invented first.

questions.text: Which office processes all local IP filings, trademark registrations, and patent reviews in the Philippines?
options: Intellectual Property Office of the Philippines (IPOPHL)
questions.explanation: The Central Authority is IPOPHL, the primary regulatory office governing all IP rights, registrations, and enforcement across the country.

questions.text: University tech built with public grants (e.g., DOST) is governed by the Philippine Technology Transfer Act of 2009, Republic Act No. ___.
questions.explanation: Academic spinoffs built with public grants are governed by the Philippine Tech Transfer Act of 2009 (RA 10055).

questions.text: Before raising private VC investment, founders of an academic spinoff must clear ownership with which office?
options: The university's Technology Licensing Office (TLO) or Innovation and Technology Support Office (ITSO)
questions.explanation: Academic spinoffs must clear ownership with the university's TLO or ITSO prior to raising private VC investment.

questions.text: Which ecosystem programs does the module name for founders to access subsidized education and legal assistance on securing digital assets?
questions.explanation: Founders can leverage programs like the WIPO-IPOPHL Summer School and the IP Management Clinic.

questions.text: Match each UST IP and innovation unit to its description.
allChoices: The university's localized IP unit and official patent library, established in 2009
The official Technology Business Incubator (TBI), established in 2019 with DOST-PCIEERD support
A dedicated facility for deep-tech and large-scale industrial collaborations outside Manila

pairs.match: The university's localized IP unit and official patent library, established in 2009
The official Technology Business Incubator (TBI), established in 2019 with DOST-PCIEERD support
A dedicated facility for deep-tech and large-scale industrial collaborations outside Manila

questions.explanation: UST-ITSO is the IP unit and patent library (2009). TOMASInno Center is the official TBI (2019, DOST-PCIEERD). UST-TTCIC handles deep-tech and industrial collaborations at the Santa Rosa campus.

questions.text: Where is the UST-TTCIC located, and who is it named after?
options: Blessed Pier Giorgio Frassati, O.P. Building along España Blvd.; named after a Dominican priest
UST Main Building in Manila; named after the university founder
UST Santa Rosa Campus in Laguna; named after alumnus Dr. Tony Tan Caktiong
UST Legazpi Campus; named after a DOST secretary
questions.explanation: UST-TTCIC is at the UST Santa Rosa Campus in Laguna, named after alumnus Dr. Tony Tan Caktiong. The Frassati Building along España Blvd. houses the TOMASInno Center.

questions.text: Which of the following does the TOMASInno Center provide or host?
options: Official patent drafting and commercial licensing
questions.explanation: TOMASInno Center provides coworking spaces, prototyping labs, pitch coaching, and hosts events like Hackathom/Innovathom for MVPs. Patent drafting, IP evaluation, and commercial licensing are handled by UST-ITSO.

questions.text: UST-ITSO's commercialization work (patent drafting, IP evaluation, and commercial licensing) is funded by what?
questions.explanation: UST-ITSO's commercialization is funded by the DOST-PCIEERD IMPACT grant.

questions.text: Match each IPR case to the lesson it highlights.

Software commercialization, sales liability, and copyright law

questions.explanation: Waymo vs. Uber: trade secret theft during employee transitions. Centripetal vs. Cisco: startup vs. legacy giant. JGC vs. Sillano: the software lockout case. MEPS vs. BTI and ETAP: the automated payment machine clone. NBI-Microsoft vs. Beltron: software distribution and copyright. Winklevoss v. Zuckerberg: the Facebook precedent.

questions.text: In Waymo vs. Uber, what did Anthony Levandowski take before resigning from Google's Waymo?
options: The source code of Google Maps
questions.explanation: Levandowski downloaded 14,000+ confidential design files (10 GB) before resigning. He launched Otto, which Uber acquired for $680M.

questions.text: Waymo vs. Uber: match each detail to its figure.
allChoices: $245M in equity
18 months in prison
10 GB

pairs.term: Price Uber paid to acquire Otto

pairs.match: $245M in equity

pairs.term: Levandowski's criminal sentence for trade secret theft
pairs.match: 18 months in prison

pairs.term: Size of the trade secrets extracted
pairs.match: 10 GB

questions.explanation: Uber acquired Otto for $680M. In 2018 Uber settled mid-trial by transferring $245M in equity and agreeing not to use Waymo's LiDAR tech. Levandowski was sentenced to 18 months in prison (later pardoned) and filed for bankruptcy. He had extracted 10 GB of trade secrets.

questions.text: In Centripetal Networks vs. Cisco, under what protection did Centripetal pitch its proprietary technology to Cisco?
questions.explanation: Centripetal pitched its proprietary network threat intelligence systems to Cisco during preliminary partnership meetings under an NDA. Cisco then integrated the exact technical methodology into its own security architectures.

questions.text: How much did a federal judge initially order Cisco to pay Centripetal Networks?
questions.explanation: A federal judge initially ordered Cisco to pay $1.9 billion in damages, one of the largest patent payouts in history. The case remains in ongoing appeals due to legal technicalities.

questions.text: In JGC Philippines vs. Sillano (2024), what did the Supreme Court rule?
options: Builders cannot sabotage or lock an enterprise out of code built during employment, so JGC's suspension was upheld
Sillano owned the software because he wrote it
JGC had to pay Sillano royalties for the software
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court (2024) upheld JGC's suspension. Builders cannot sabotage or lock an enterprise out of code built during employment. A code lockout constitutes illegal sabotage.

questions.text: What startup action does the JGC Philippines vs. Sillano case recommend?
options: Register all source code as a trademark
Implement Day-1 Proprietary Information and Inventions Agreements (PIIAs) for all developers
Never let developers have admin access
questions.explanation: The startup action is to implement Day-1 Proprietary Information and Inventions Agreements (PIIAs) for all developers.

questions.text: In MEPS vs. BTI and ETAP, which body ruled in MEPS's favor, and how much was BTI directed to pay?
options: The Philippine Dispute Resolution Center (PDRCI); ₱5.3M in damages
questions.explanation: MEPS, creator of TouchPay kiosks, sued under registered Utility Model rights over BTI's "Pay&Go" clones made by ETAP. The Philippine Dispute Resolution Center (PDRCI) ruled in MEPS's favor in a 2022 arbitral award and directed BTI to pay ₱5.3M in damages.

questions.text: What is the takeaway from MEPS vs. BTI and ETAP for hardware and IoT startups?
options: Hardware can't be protected, so focus on software
Early registration of Utility Models or Patents provides enforceable market defense against rapid copying
Keep all hardware designs as trade secrets only
Rely on copyright alone for physical devices
questions.explanation: Hardware and IoT startups face rapid copying. Early registration of Utility Models or Patents (an IPOPHL filing) provides enforceable market defense.

questions.text: In NBI-Microsoft Corporation vs. Beltron Computer (G.R. No. 147043), what did the Supreme Court rule?
options: Selling hardware with pre-loaded software is not infringement unless the vendor is caught burning the copies
Microsoft had no copyright over pre-installed software
Unauthorized distribution and commercial sale on its own constitutes copyright infringement
The Court of Appeals' decision was upheld in full
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court reversed the CA, ruling that unauthorized distribution and commercial sale on its own constitutes copyright infringement. There is no need to catch the vendor writing or burning code.

questions.text: What is the technopreneur takeaway from NBI-Microsoft vs. Beltron Computer for SaaS and app ventures?
options: Your EULA and distribution loops must explicitly set licensing limits to avoid direct liability when bundling software
Copyright only applies to hardware vendors
questions.explanation: For SaaS and app ventures, your EULA and distribution loops must explicitly set licensing limits, and you must ensure valid commercial authorization (a master license) for third-party tech.

questions.text: How did Zuckerberg settle the dispute with the Winklevoss twins?
options: By paying them $65 million in cash and Facebook stock
questions.explanation: Zuckerberg settled by paying the Winklevoss twins $65 million in cash and Facebook stock. Because the original partnership boundaries over HarvardConnection were vague, a massive legal battle ensued.

questions.text: What is the startup takeaway from Winklevoss v. Zuckerberg?
options: Define co-founder IP assignment and equity from Day 1
questions.explanation: The vulnerability was a vague initial agreement and informal partnership terms. The takeaway: define co-founder IP assignment and equity from Day 1.

questions.text: Under the IPOPHL Intellectual Property Code, copyright on a capstone paper and its source code is automatic the moment it is written or saved, with no official certificate needed to prove authorship.
questions.explanation: Copyright protection is automatic the moment your group writes the paper or saves code to a drive. No official certificate is required to prove authorship.

questions.text: If a capstone group built a physical device or specialized hardware prototype, how is its underlying function protected?
options: It requires a formal patent or utility model filing
Automatically, once the capstone is defended
questions.explanation: The underlying function of a physical device, hardware prototype, or advanced process is not automatically protected. It requires a formal patent or utility model filing and is highly vulnerable to replication if disclosed early.

questions.text: Match each trigger for shifting from an "academic mindset" to an "IPR filing mindset" to its description.
allChoices: Planning to commercialize after graduation, so you should file before any public showcase
Presenting at innovation fairs, institutional repositories, or open hackathons, which destroys novelty
Using major campus labs, which requires IP review through the university's ITSO

pairs.match: Planning to commercialize after graduation, so you should file before any public showcase
Presenting at innovation fairs, institutional repositories, or open hackathons, which destroys novelty
Using major campus labs, which requires IP review through the university's ITSO

questions.explanation: Startup Ambitions: file the patent prior to public defense, since the Philippines follows a strict First-to-File system. Public Disclosure: review IP status before external events. University Policy: projects using major campus labs go through ITSO review, and schools may sponsor filing fees for high-value tech.

questions.text: The Co-Ownership Trap: match each capstone situation to who holds the IP.
allChoices: The student group retains commercialization control
The university legally co-owns the IP
The rights belong to the sponsoring company

pairs.term: Idea fully conceptualized by students and built without specialized campus equipment
pairs.match: The student group retains commercialization control

pairs.term: Built using specialized school labs, proprietary datasets, or university funding
pairs.match: The university legally co-owns the IP

pairs.term: Solved a problem for an industry sponsor, with an IP Assignment Waiver signed
pairs.match: The rights belong to the sponsoring company

questions.explanation: Independent ideas stay with the student group. Use of university resources makes the university a co-owner, needing joint IP clearance. Sponsored capstones usually involve an IP Assignment Waiver transferring rights to the company.

questions.text: Before spending money filing an independent application with IPOPHL for a capstone, what should students verify first?
options: Whether the project won a hackathon
The number of downloads of their app
questions.explanation: Before you spend money filing an independent application with IPOPHL, verify your university's Student IP Policy.
